# QS-CFW-4713-78 Quality specification - axle hub CFW-4713-78 (4140)

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P2  
Parts: CFW-4713-78

Scope
- This quality specification applies to the manufactured axle hub identified as CFW-4713-78, forged from material designated 4140 at Plant P2. It defines acceptance criteria, mandatory inspection methods, records to retain, and the nonconformance handling process for production, finishing, and final inspection prior to release to shipping or assembly.
- The intent is to ensure consistent mechanical properties and dimensional conformity for service use. Background rationale: the chosen hardness and bore tolerance reflect required performance for fitment and wear life while the maximum forging weight limit is to ensure safe material handling and appropriate process controls during forging and heat treatment.

Requirements table
- The following table lists mandatory acceptance criteria. These criteria are to be applied to every lot presented for final inspection. Where values are stated, they are mandatory and testing or measuring equipment shall be calibrated to national or internal standards; records of calibration shall accompany inspection records.

| Characteristic | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Material | 4140 (as specified on part drawing and heat treat route) |
| Hardness (post-process) | The hardness range for axle hub CFW-4713-78 (CFW-4713-78) is 29-32 HRC. |
| Bore diameter tolerance | The bore diameter tolerance for axle hub CFW-4713-78 (CFW-4713-78) is ±0.04 mm. |
| Maximum forging weight | The maximum forging weight for axle hub CFW-4713-78 (CFW-4713-78) is 106.1 kg. |
| Surface condition | Free of laps, cracks, and foreign inclusions that affect function (visual and tactile confirmation) |
| Threaded features and mating faces | Must meet drawing geometry and be free of galling and burrs that prevent assembly |

Inspection method
- Visual inspection
  - Perform a visual assessment under standard shop lighting to detect surface discontinuities, laps, scale, or other defects. Use magnification when necessary to clarify questionable features. Record observations on the final inspection form.
- Dimensional inspection
  - Measure bore diameter using a calibrated bore gauge or internal micrometer capable of resolving the stated tolerance. Verify conformity to the bore diameter tolerance for axle hub CFW-4713-78 (CFW-4713-78) is ±0.04 mm. When measuring, ensure gauge contact surfaces are clean and gauge temperature has stabilized to ambient shop conditions.
  - Measure other drawing-controlled dimensions as applicable to confirm fit. Use calibrated instruments and capture raw readings and instrument identification on the inspection record.
- Hardness testing
  - Test hardness in the machined, finished condition at locations specified on the part drawing. The hardness range for axle hub CFW-4713-78 (CFW-4713-78) is 29-32 HRC. Use a calibrated Rockwell hardness tester and follow standard test practice for the chosen indenter. Document test locations, instrument ID, operator, and individual hardness readings on the inspection record.
- Weight verification
  - Confirm forging weight does not exceed the maximum forging weight for axle hub CFW-4713-78 (CFW-4713-78) is 106.1 kg. Use calibrated scales and include scale ID and weight reading on the material handling record. If the forging weight approaches the maximum, tag and segregate the part pending engineering disposition.
- Sampling and acceptance
  - Inspection shall follow the inspection plan for the part. When sampling is used for lot acceptance, ensure the sampling rationale and results are documented and justified in the lot record. Any measured value outside the stated requirement is a nonconformance.

Nonconformance handling
- Identification and segregation
  - Any unit that fails to meet the hardness range, bore diameter tolerance, maximum forging weight, or other drawing requirement must be clearly identified and physically segregated from conforming product. Use the nonconforming product tag and store in a designated quarantine area.
- Documentation
  - Complete a nonconformance report that includes part identification, manufacturing lot or heat number, description of nonconformance, measured values, inspection records, and photographs where useful. Reference the inspection record and equipment calibration entries that produced the measurement.
- Disposition options
  - Notify quality engineering and production supervision immediately for review. Disposition may include rework where permitted by engineering, return to heat treatment or machining if allowed by the process control plan, use-as-is only with documented customer approval, or scrap. Any rework must be carried out per documented procedures and followed by reinspection.
- Root cause and corrective action
  - For confirmed nonconformances, perform a root cause analysis and document corrective actions. Include process step controls or inspection additions intended to prevent recurrence. Record effectiveness checks in the quality system records.

Records to keep
- Final inspection report with instrument IDs, operator initials, and actual hardness readings at each test location. Ensure the hardness range for axle hub CFW-4713-78 (CFW-4713-78) is clearly referenced.
- Dimensional inspection records showing bore measurements and confirmation that the bore diameter tolerance for axle hub CFW-4713-78 (CFW-4713-78) is ±0.04 mm.
- Material and forging weight records including scale ID and verification that the maximum forging weight for axle hub CFW-4713-78 (CFW-4713-78) is 106.1 kg.
- Calibration certificates for all measuring equipment used and operator training records for inspection personnel.
- Nonconformance reports and corrective action records associated with this part number.

Examples and step rationale
- Example: a hub presented with a bore measurement outside the stated tolerance must be tagged and held. Rationale: bore fit affects bearing seating and axial runout; immediate segregation avoids downstream assembly failures.
- Example: a hardness test yielding a reading below the specified range requires review of heat treat records. Rationale: hardness correlates to strength and fatigue life; correcting the thermal process or segregating the material prevents field failures.
- Example: a forging exceeding the maximum forging weight is handled as a handling and process control risk. Rationale: tooling and material flow are validated up to the stated maximum; heavier forgings may not meet process assumptions and can cause tool damage or process variability.

Approval and responsibilities
- Production is responsible for initial inspection and identification. Quality is responsible for final disposition and record retention. Engineering provides dispositions for rework and approves any deviations.

End of document.
